sentences.text: It is submitted that matter may be heard on it's merits.

2. This is the first bail application filed on behalf of the applicants/accused under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail, as they are under apprehension of arrest, in connection with Private Complaint Case No.RTC337/2020 pending before Judicial Magistrate First Class Satna District-Satna (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B of Indian Penal Code.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First Class Satna District-Satna
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel appearing for the applicant submitted that co-accused in the case namely Dashrath Agrawal, who is said to have forged the will, has already been released on anticipatory bail in M.Cr.C.No.28925/2022 vide order dated 29.07.2022.
It is submitted that applicants' case stands on a better footing.
In these circumstances, applicants may not be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
4. Learned Govt. Advocate appearing for the State formally opposed the application for grant of anticipatory bail.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
6.
Other co-accused persons namely Dashrash Agrawal, Ranjana, Brajendra and Shailendra Agrawal were released on bail by this Court.
Case of applicants is similar to that of co-accused person.
7. Considering the same and on grounds of parity, anticipatory bail application filed by the applicants is allowed.

It is directed that in the event of arrest of applicants in connection with the aforesaid crime number and the offences, he be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rs.Fifty Thousand only) each with one solvent surety each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer/Arresting Authority.
8. The applicants are directed to join the investigation immediately and to co-operate with the investigating agency.

They will further abide by the condition enumerated in sub-section (2) of Section 438 of the Cr.P.C.
Certified copy as per rules.
